## Part 3 — `relevanceDef` and the relevance gate it drives

### The disease (verified in code)

- **The escalation trigger thresholds the WRONG NUMBER.** `_unsure` is byte-identical in all six cascades (`instagram/cascade.py:150-160`, `x:103-109`, `linkedin:101-107`, `reddit:90-96`, `telegram:89-95`, `youtube:89-95`) and its score arm is `abs(decision.score - campaign.threshold) < 0.05`. `campaign.threshold` is the MATCH cutoff (default 0.70, `core/config.py:391`); the relevance boundary is `RELEVANCE_GATE = 0.5`. ⚠️ Verified by running the real `_unsure` against the real Tashkent campaign (band `[0.40, 0.65]`, threshold 0.70): score 0.45/0.48/0.50/0.52/0.55 → `unsure=False` at BOTH confidence 0.30 and 0.90; score 0.66/0.70/0.74 → `unsure=True` at both. A reel one hundredth below the gate is rejected forever on one caption call and never sees vision, STT, video or escalation; a reel 0.20 clear of the gate pays for the whole ladder to re-confirm what was never in doubt. **Scope honestly:** this changes only when an escalation call is SPENT, not the verdict — the verdict at `:327` already uses `RELEVANCE_GATE`.
- **The shipped relevance prompt promises an escalation the code cannot deliver.** `IG_RELEVANCE` (`engines/instagram/prompts.py:141-144`) instructs a borderline score (0.40–0.55) "so the engine can escalate to the video instead of guessing confidently"; `VISION_GENERIC` (`core/prompts.py:37-38`) says the same. **Nothing in `_unsure` reads 0.40–0.55.** On the shipped Acme campaign (band `[0.40, 0.75]`) a verdict of score 0.48 / confidence 0.85 returns `unsure=False` — verified. The prompt-code contract is broken in exactly the case the prompt was written for.
- **The label-wins-over-score rule inverts on capitalisation and whitespace.** `relevant = d.score >= RELEVANCE_GATE if d.label not in {"relevant","irrelevant"} else d.label == "relevant"` (`instagram/cascade.py:327-328` + five twins) compares the RAW string, while `_decision_from_payload` stores it unnormalised (`core/router.py:293`) and `_has_usable_verdict` — 20 lines earlier at `:271-273` — strips and lowercases. ⚠️ Verified by executing the real parser: `{"label":"Irrelevant","score":0.9}` → **relevant=True**; `{"label":" relevant ","score":0.1}` → **relevant=False**. Both inverted by formatting the model chose, with no log line distinguishing them.
- **The router guarantees NOTHING about label/score consistency, and the label is an unvalidated channel a MODEL-AUTHORED prompt can use to move the decision boundary.** `_decision_from_payload` clamps score to [0,1] and defaults a missing score to 0.0; it never cross-checks. `generate_advanced_prompts` writes the campaign's `relevancePrompt` with a model, validated only by `_prompt_carries_contract` (`campaign_gen.py:883-889`), which does **not** pin the label vocabulary to {relevant, irrelevant} and does not know `RELEVANCE_GATE` exists. A generated prompt saying `label="relevant" iff score>=0.7` passes and silently raises the gate to 0.70; one saying `"label":"yes"|"no"` passes and disables the label rule entirely. Neither is recorded anywhere.
- **A cloud outage is written into the corpus as a permanent content judgment.** `_degrade` returns `Decision(label="unknown", score=0.0, confidence=0.0, tier="degraded")` (`router.py:647`). `_unsure` catches `tier == "degraded"` and escalates **once** (`instagram/cascade.py:316-325`), then computes `relevant` from whatever came back. ⚠️ Verified end-to-end with the real `Cascade` and a router that degrades every call: `gate_reel` → `relevant=False, escalated=True` after 2 calls. `session.py` then writes `mark_seen(relevant=gate.relevant)` and `store.is_seen` (`store.py:1622-1628`) is a bare existence check — `grep 'DELETE FROM seen_reels'` returns nothing. Every reel of a run made during a key/credit/model outage is blacklisted for that campaign forever behind a soft `cloud_degraded` flag.
- **A thin caption with no frames produces a confident reject, contradicting the docstring.** `gate_reel`'s docstring says "a no-text caption must not produce a confident reject" (`instagram/cascade.py:211-212`), but the `else` branch at `:254-257` sends the empty caption to `classify_text` when `frames()` is empty. ⚠️ Verified: caption `"🔥🔥 #remont"` with no frames → 1 call, `relevant=False`. The escalation re-ask sends the same empty caption again.
- **Escalation discards every tier of evidence the ladder just paid for** — see Sheet #4. Unchanged from Sheet #3's flag at the old line numbers.
- **Relevance persists as a bare boolean.** `seen_reels` (`store.py:159-176`) has `relevant INTEGER`, `video_analyzed` and `video_analysis_summary` — no score, reason, tier, confidence, escalated flag or model. `mark_seen`'s signature (`:1630-1639`) has nowhere to put them. `RelevanceResult` (`instagram/cascade.py:54-61` + twins) carries `decision`, `used_vision`, `used_stt`, `used_video`, `escalated` — every session drops all of it except `used_video`. Contrast `matches`, which keeps `score`, `reason`, `tier` (`store.py:145-149`). No flip-list substrate, no way to re-sweep a cutoff offline.
- **Relevance false-negatives are laundered into a permanent cross-campaign seed blacklist.** `source_stats` derives `relevant_reels` from `seen_reels WHERE relevant=1` (`store.py:1741-1743`); `park_dry_sources` parks on `navigations >= 3 AND yielded >= 30 AND not relevant_reels` (`:1794-1799`); `seed_history` feeds `_seed_feedback_block`, which renders dead seeds as "Do NOT propose them or close variants" — explicitly "a hard MUST NOT" per its own docstring. **A mis-tuned gate does not just lose reels: it parks the seed, then teaches the generator never to propose that vocabulary again for this tenant on this platform.**
- **`relevanceDef` gets no supply-side-exclusion analogue and no validation anywhere.** `SYSTEM_CAMPAIGN_GEN` (`core/prompts.py:69-70`) asks for "1-3 sentences defining what makes a Reel/post ON-TOPIC" — positives only. The very next key, `matchDef`, carries a mandatory exclusion clause enforced in code by `_ensure_supply_side_exclusion` (`campaign_gen.py:558-572`, applied at `:615` and `:951`). Nothing does that for relevance. The fallback is `f"Public posts, videos, and discussions about {topic}."` (`:946`). Server-side, `_BRIEF_BLANK_DROP_KEYS` covers only the three prompts (`server.py:851-853`), so a blank `relevanceDef` overwrites a good one and persists as `""` — `core/config.py:462` reads it with no check, and `USER_TEMPLATE` then sends `CAMPAIGN BRIEF:\n\n` to the model.
- **A prose `relevanceDef` silently disables warming's relevance filter.** `WarmingActionExecutor._relevance_tokens` tokenises `seed_hashtags + seed_accounts + relevance_def` with `_TOKEN_RE = [#@]?[\w]+` and **no stopword list** (`engines/warming/executor.py:56, 93-95`), and `_is_relevant` returns True on any single shared token (`:109-117`). The generated fallback tokenises to {public, posts, videos, and, discussions, about, `<topic>`} — so every reel whose caption contains "and" or "about" is treated as on-topic. `relevanceDef` has a second, non-LLM consumer whose failure mode is the exact opposite of the gate's.
- **The eval harness measures a decision rule production does not use.** `scripts/eval/run_eval.py:146` computes `pred = score >= cfg["cutoff"]` with `cutoff: 0.5` hard-coded at `:57` — score-only, no label rule, no `_unsure`, no vision/STT/video tier, single call. ⚠️ Worse, `score_one` (`:68-83`) calls `router._post` directly, bypassing `_spend_guard`, `_record`, `_degrade`, the `_CallBudget` and the JSON-mode latch, and hardcodes `usd=0.0`. The gold set is **20 items, all `lang: "en"`** (measured), 10 positive / 10 negative, while production's observed base rate in the 2026-08-19 shakedown was 1 relevance pass in 25 reels (`memory/known-issues.md:1441`): at TPR 0.9 / FPR 0.1 a balanced set reports precision 0.90 while the same classifier at 4% prevalence delivers 0.27.
- **Six byte-identical copies of everything.** `RELEVANCE_GATE`, `_unsure`, `RelevanceResult` and the label rule are duplicated across all six cascades (line numbers above). `core/matching.py` already exists as the shared home for exactly this kind of decision helper (`ground_extracted:26`, `corroboration_needs_review:63`) and is imported by Instagram only.

### Remedy A — Fix the escalation trigger: thresh the gate the stage actually uses

Give `_unsure` the cutoff the CALLING STAGE decides on instead of always reading `campaign.threshold`: `_unsure(decision, campaign, *, cutoff)`, called with `RELEVANCE_GATE` from every `gate_*` and with `campaign.threshold` from every `score_comment`. ~17 call sites, 6 files, no signature change reaching the router or any test double. Hoist the single implementation into `core/matching.py` alongside `corroboration_needs_review` — the precedent is there and the import is one line per cascade.

Widening the relevance straddle band to 0.05 either side of 0.50 gives 0.45–0.55, which is exactly the interval `IG_RELEVANCE` and `VISION_GENERIC` already instruct the model to park ambiguous verdicts in — so prompt and code finally agree.

**Effort:** 0.5 day. **Risk:** escalation volume shifts — reels near 0.50 start escalating (they should) and reels near 0.70 stop (they never should have). Net relevance-stage spend likely RISES on the Tashkent brief, whose narrowed `[0.40,0.65]` band was tuned against the broken trigger. Re-tune the band after, not before.

### Remedy B — Normalise the label once, in the router; make the decision rule explicit and shared

In `_decision_from_payload` (`core/router.py:293`) store `str(p.get("label","unknown")).strip().lower()` — matching what `_has_usable_verdict` already does 20 lines above. Then replace the six copies of the ternary with one `core/matching.relevance_verdict(decision, gate) -> tuple[bool, str]` returning the verdict AND the rule that produced it (`"label"` / `"score"` / `"conflict"`), so the reason is loggable and persistable.

Keep label-wins as the DEFAULT, but flag the conflict case: label says relevant and score < gate (or the inverse) by more than a small epsilon.

**Effort:** 0.5 day. **Risk:** lowercasing is observable by anything comparing `d.label` case-sensitively — grep shows only the six ternaries and log formatting, but `matches.tier` / `found_by_models` paths should be re-checked. A campaign whose model emitted "Irrelevant" will see its verdicts flip (correctly), which will look like a regression in per-source yield.

### Remedy C — Persist the relevance verdict as a row, not a bit (schema v26)

Additive columns on `seen_reels` via the v18/v19/v24/v25 `_add_column_if_missing` idiom (`store.py:1367-1405`): `relevance_score REAL`, `relevance_confidence REAL`, `relevance_reason TEXT`, `relevance_tier TEXT`, `relevance_rule TEXT` (Remedy B), `relevance_tiers TEXT` (compact JSON of used_vision/used_stt/used_video/escalated — data `RelevanceResult` already carries and every session throws away), `relevance_model TEXT`, `gated_at REAL`. Thread through the six `mark_seen(relevant=gate.relevant, …)` sites — the same mechanical edit v24 and v25 each made. Nothing new is computed.

Then make `is_seen` (`store.py:1622`) refuse to treat `relevance_tier='degraded'` as a settled verdict, so an outage-poisoned reel is re-gated on the next run; the `COALESCE` in `mark_seen:1656` already supports the overwrite.

**Effort:** 1–1.5 days. **Risk:** widening `is_seen` means a post-outage run re-walks reels it has seen — desired, but it changes the dedupe watermark's contract, which three engines and `already_seen_skips` depend on. Gate it **strictly** on `relevance_tier='degraded'`, never on a low score, or the watermark stops working.

### Remedy D — `_ensure_near_miss_exclusion`: the relevance-side analogue of `_ensure_supply_side_exclusion`

The discriminator relevance needs is not demand-vs-supply, it is **OBJECT-vs-VERB** — the pattern the Tashkent brief already discovered and wrote by hand at `tashkent-renovation.md:131-136`, `:197`: *"Find the OBJECT, not the verb. The words «ремонт», «ta'mirlash», «remont» alone prove NOTHING — they cover cars, phones, appliances and watches in exactly the same spelling."*

Concretely: (1) extend `SYSTEM_CAMPAIGN_GEN`'s `relevanceDef` spec to require three parts — the on-topic OBJECT, 3–6 concrete positive content types, and an explicit NOT-RELEVANT list naming the near-misses that share the campaign's own vocabulary; (2) add `_ensure_near_miss_exclusion(relevance_def)` mirroring the marker-scan/append shape of its supply-side twin; (3) apply it at both `assemble_draft` (`campaign_gen.py:627`) and `_ensure_minimum_defs` (`:946`), the two places `matchDef` already gets its clause. Ask the generator for a `nearMissTerms` array too — the same shape `seedNouns` uses — so the exclusion list is **data**, not only prose.

**Effort:** 1 day. **Risk:** the near-miss list is only as good as the model's knowledge of the vertical. Mitigate the way `_ensure_supply_side_exclusion` does (conservative marker detection; redundant appends harmless) and make the operator's edit authoritative. Real precision/recall tension: an over-broad exclusion list is itself a false-negative generator, and false negatives here are invisible (Remedy F).

### Remedy E — Make `relevanceDef` prose safe for its SECOND consumer (warming)

Two independent cheap fixes: (1) drop tokens shorter than 4 chars and a small per-language stopword set before building `_relevance_tokens` — warming is forbidden from router/LLM calls (`engines/warming/session.py:11-13`) so this must stay heuristic-only; (2) prefer the structured `nearMissTerms`/`seedNouns` arrays from Remedy D over free prose as the token source. Add a test that the shipped fallback `relevanceDef` does NOT make `_is_relevant` return True for an obviously off-topic caption.

**Effort:** 0.5 day. **Risk:** warming is hard-stop-gated (`AIZU_WARMING_ENABLED`, default off); a stricter filter means fewer warming actions fire — the point, but it changes the account-warming rate the pool math assumes.

### Remedy F — Set the operating point where the asymmetry actually is: recall-first at the gate, precision at the match

Sheet #3's rule for match is "max precision s.t. recall ≥ 0.9." Relevance must be tuned the other way and the code should encode it. (1) Sweep `RELEVANCE_GATE` with `core/evalstats.sweep_threshold` for **max recall s.t. precision ≥ p**, choosing p from the measured downstream cost per admitted reel rather than a round number. (2) Promote `RELEVANCE_GATE` from a module constant to `campaign.relevance_gate` with the same `0 < g < 1` bridge validation Sheet #3 added for threshold (`server.py:739-747`) and the same `campaign_gen` clamp (`:611`), so it is sweepable per campaign and the generated relevance prompt can have it templated in the way `ig_match(threshold)` does. (3) **Capture rejects** — sample sub-gate reels into an `eval_candidates`-style table so the FN rate is estimable at all.

Rationale: a relevance FP costs one browser open plus N match calls and is fully recoverable; a relevance FN is permanent and compounding (parks the seed, blacklists the vocabulary).

**Effort:** 1 day for the sweep + validation plumbing; the reject-capture rides on Remedy C. **Risk:** loosening the gate raises match-stage spend and browser wall-clock linearly and burns the 20–40 reel/session budget (`core/pacing.py:36-37`) faster. Only tunable once rejects are sampled and the gold set is real — **do not move the constant on the 20-item English gold set.**

### Remedy G — Give escalation the evidence the ladder already paid for

Build the escalation content the way `_comment_content` (`instagram/cascade.py:95-114`) already builds the match content — caption + `reel.ocr_text` + `reel.transcript` + `reel.video_analysis` — so the second look is strictly more informed than the first, not a byte-identical re-ask. This is the cheapest half of Sheet #3's Remedy F and, unlike the k=5 sampled vote, it does NOT violate the single-budget rule because it is still one call. It already goes through `_HeartbeatRouter` (same `self.router`).

**Effort:** 0.5 day. **Risk:** a longer payload costs more input tokens on exactly the reels that already cost the most. Bounded and worth it — the alternative is paying for STT and video frames and then not showing them to the model that decides.

### Remedy H — Pin the generated `relevancePrompt`'s label vocabulary and gate agreement

Add a per-key contract to `_prompt_carries_contract` (`campaign_gen.py:883-889`): the relevance and vision prompts must contain both `"relevant"` and `"irrelevant"` (the only two literals the gate special-cases), and must not state a numeric cutoff other than the campaign's own — or better, TEMPLATE the gate in the way Sheet #3 templated the threshold into `ig_match()`. Drop-on-failure is already the behaviour, so the failure mode is the vertical-neutral fallback.

**Effort:** 0.5 day. **Risk:** more generated prompts get dropped and more campaigns run on the neutral fallback. That is the correct trade — Sheet #3's IG finding was that a WRONG shipped prompt is worse than a generic one — but it reads to an operator as "the AI stopped filling in the Advanced section." Surface the drop.

### Remedy I — Rebuild the relevance harness to replay the real decision path

Extract the label rule (byte-identical across all six cascades) into the shared `core/matching.relevance_verdict` from Remedy B and have both the harness and all six gates call it, so harness and production cannot diverge again. Drive the harness through the real `Cascade.gate_reel` on a store-less `OpenRouterRouter(store=None)`.

The store-less plumbing works with **zero code change** — `_spend_guard` returns True at `router.py:621-624`, `_record` no-ops at `:634-638`, `_degrade`'s `raise_flag` at `:642`, `log_model_comparison` at `:812`; every `self.store` use is None-guarded. ⚠️ But **two harness capabilities DO need code**, contrary to the "zero code change" framing:
- **Cost/item must come from a counting router wrapper** summing `Decision.usd`. `cascade.escalations` is only an escalation COUNTER, `gate_reel` overwrites `d` at every tier so only the LAST call's usd survives on `RelevanceResult.decision`, and with `store=None` `_record` no-ops entirely.
- **The variant `USER_TEMPLATE` axis needs an injectable user template.** `_build_text_payload` uses the `USER_TEMPLATE` bound into `core/router.py` at import (`:30`), while `variants_relevance/current_relevance.py:11` and `v2_relevance.py:36-42` each define their own. Without injection, variants silently collapse to system-prompt-only.

⚠️ Also scope the claim: with caption-only gold and no `frame_b64`/`capture_fn`/`transcribe_fn`/`video_analyze_fn`, `frames()` returns `[]` and the vision/STT/video tiers **cannot fire** (`config/campaign.md:38` also sets `enable_stt: false`). The replay exercises caption → escalation → label rule, not the whole ladder. The vision tiers stay dark until the gold set carries frame fixtures (Sheet #4).

Gold set v1 needs Sheet #3's **actual** discipline: ≥30 items per language/script slice, transliteration pairs, and **ENRICHED** strata (~25% easy pos / 25% easy neg / 30% hard neg / 10% boundary, ~35% positive) with the production base rate measured from `seen_reels.relevant` and used to **reweight** reported precision — ⚠️ not used as the sampling rate. Sampling at the natural ~4% rate starves a 150–200 item set of positives; standard practice is to oversample thin strata and reweight stratum metrics by production proportions.

**Effort:** 1–2 days (harness); the gold set is a separate labelling decision. **Risk:** the two per-router latches (`_json_mode`, `_degraded`) — one router per variant, abort on degraded runs. A degraded run through the real `gate_reel` now returns `relevant=False` for every item, which would read as a catastrophic recall regression rather than an outage.

### Deliberately excluded (relevance)

- **Deleting the label rule outright (score-only).** Tempting after the capitalisation inversion, but wrong: `_decision_from_payload` defaults a MISSING score to 0.0 with `tier="cloud"`, and `_has_usable_verdict` deliberately treats a stated label as authoritative and lets `{"label":"relevant"}` with no score through (`router.py:263-267` — its docstring records that reading the two keys as an OR was the shakedown bug). Score-only turns every score-omitting reply into a confident reject: bug H3 (`memory/known-issues.md:1490-1500`) reintroduced through a different door. Normalise the label (Remedy B) rather than remove it.
- **Keeping label-wins unconditionally, as today.** The argument FOR it is real and should be recorded: `label` is a discrete commitment and `score` is a verbalised scalar, and Sheet #3's rubric literature (~45% calibration error, occasional inverse correlation with accuracy) says the scalar is the less trustworthy of the two. The argument AGAINST is stronger and specific to this codebase: the router guarantees nothing about their consistency, the label is a string a MODEL-AUTHORED prompt chooses with only a substring check between it and production, and a generated prompt saying `label="relevant" iff score>=0.7` moves the effective gate from 0.50 to 0.70 with no record anywhere. **Verdict:** keep label-wins as the default, but treat a wide label/score disagreement as a THIRD outcome (unsure → escalate, persist `relevance_rule='conflict'`), not a silent win for either side. A model returning label=relevant with score=0.2 is not a decision, it is a self-contradiction, and the one thing the code must not do is pick a side quietly.
- **Making `RELEVANCE_GATE` campaign-editable before rejects are sampled.** Remedy F proposes it; it must not ship first. Sub-gate reels leave `seen_reels.relevant=0` and nothing else. Handing an operator a knob whose false-negative side is unobservable and permanent is worse than a wrong constant, because the constant is at least uniform and diagnosable.
- **A k=5 sampled vote for relevance escalation.** Ruled out by Sheet #3's constraint 1 for the same reason as match, only worse: relevance runs on **every** reel, so five calls per reel multiplies against the 20–40 reel budget. Remedy G (one better-informed call) is the affordable half.
- **Deleting from `seen_reels` / a TTL on the watermark.** A TTL would re-walk everything, not just poisoned rows, and the forward-only contract is load-bearing for `already_seen_skips` and the tired-feed canary in all six sessions. The targeted version (Remedy C) recovers the outage case without touching the contract for genuine verdicts.
- **Rebalancing the existing 20-item relevance gold set.** 100% English on a product whose live briefs are ru/uz-Latin/uz-Cyrillic, balanced 10/10 against a base rate near 4%, and measured through a decision rule production does not use. Sheet #3's statistics work already established that a set this size cannot separate signal from noise; adding items to a set with the wrong prevalence and the wrong decision rule buys precision estimates wrong by a factor of three. **Build v1 fresh, or measure nothing.**
- **A separate relevance-stage spend column.** Not needed — `spend_log.stage` already separates `relevance` / `match` / `video_analysis` and `Store.spend_by_stage` (`store.py:3339-3345`) aggregates it. The one real gap is that relevance-TEXT and relevance-VISION share `stage="relevance"` (`instagram/cascade.py:250`, `:269`), so the caption tier cannot be costed separately from the vision tier — a one-word change at two call sites (and Sheet #4 Remedy B does it), not a schema addition.

### Open questions (relevance)

1. **Where is the cost asymmetry actually, once the ladder is priced?** The premise "relevance is cheaper but runs on everything" is only half true. ⚠️ Measured on the real Tashkent campaign: a relevance TEXT call carries relevance_prompt 6,749 chars + relevance_def 1,717 + caption ≈ 9k chars in; a match call carries match_prompt 20,914 + match_def 1,738 + extract_def 832 + the whole reel-context block + comment ≈ 25k — match is ~2.8× per call. At the shakedown's observed 25 reels : 12 comments the two stages cost roughly the same in aggregate, and relevance only dominates once reels-per-scored-comment exceeds ~2.8. But that ignores the vision/STT/video tiers, which ARE relevance-stage calls and are the most expensive in the system. The question `spend_by_stage` should answer on a real run: what fraction of relevance spend is the caption tier vs the escalation ladder? If it is mostly the ladder, Remedy A is a **cost** fix, not just a correctness fix.
2. **What is the actual false-negative rate?** Unanswerable today — nothing samples sub-gate reels. Every recall claim in this part is inferred from the decision rule, not measured. Remedy C's reject capture is a prerequisite for every tuning decision in Remedy F.
3. **Should `relevanceDef` stay prose at all, or become structured?** Sheet #3's Remedy A argues the free-text-def + model-scalar design is itself the anti-pattern. The same applies here, and the object-vs-verb discriminator decomposes cleanly: `{subject_object: str, is_target_object: bool, content_type: enum, evidence: str}`. Deferred pending an operator decision, because it changes what the panel field IS, not just what it says.
4. **Does the generated `relevancePrompt` ever actually get written?** `generate_advanced_prompts` is best-effort and never raises (`campaign_gen.py:906-914`); the draft ships with `relevancePrompt: ""` (`:630`). If most campaigns run on the vertical-neutral `IG_RELEVANCE` fallback, Remedy H is low-value and Remedy D (fixing the DEF, which always reaches the model as the instruction) is where the leverage is. **One query against a real DB, and it should be run before ordering the build.**

## Build order (Sheet #5, all three parts)

1. **`_coerce_extract_def` bug fixes + the missing tests + the demo fixture** (Part 2 Remedy F) — ~0.5 day. Pure win, no behaviour risk, unblocks honest measurement of everything downstream.
2. **`core/langs.py`: canonicalizer + closed-set detector; rewire all six language consumers** (Part 1 Remedies C + D) — ~2 days. Item (4) (deterministic `hl`) and item (1) (STT gate) each fix a live bug on their own.
3. **`_unsure` cutoff parameterization + label normalization + `core/matching.relevance_verdict`, hoisted out of six cascades** (Part 3 Remedies A + B) — ~1 day. Shares the `_unsure` edit with Sheet #4 Remedy A.4 — **do them in one change or the six-file edit happens twice.**
4. **Extract-field chips in the panel + type-driven `LeadDetails` + export columns** (Part 2 Remedy E) — ~1.5 days. Makes every silent failure visible at authoring time, which is the precondition for trusting any later measurement.
5. **`_ensure_near_miss_exclusion` + `nearMissTerms` + the warming tokenizer fix** (Part 3 Remedies D + E) — ~1.5 days.
6. **Relevance verdict persistence (schema v26) + degraded-tier re-gating** (Part 3 Remedy C) — ~1.5 days. Prerequisite for every tuning decision.
7. **Typed extract-field spec + span-grounded extraction + `phonenumberslite`** (Part 2 Remedies A + B + C) — ~4.5 days. Do this **with** Sheet #3 step 3's output-contract redesign, not after it.
8. **Detected `language_profile` + exemplar plumbing** (Part 1 Remedies A + E + F) — ~2 days, after the first live run gives it a corpus.
9. **Relevance harness replay + `aizu fields`** (Part 3 Remedy I, Part 2 Remedy D) — ~2 days, gated on the gold set.

~16–17 days for the whole sheet, of which steps 1–3 (~3.5 days) are strict bug fixes that pay back immediately.
